items.question_text: What will Anthropic (ANT) close at on Friday, November 27, 2026?
items.background_info:
Anthropic, PBC has never had a public market for its Class A common stock, and as of 13 November 2026 the shares do not yet trade. Its amended IPO filing (S-1/A No. 2, filed 10 November 2026) set an estimated initial public offering price of $70.00–$78.00 per share for 825,000,000 Class A shares, and the company applied to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker "ANT" (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2130357/000162828026072484/anthropicpbc-sx1ax2.htm). The offering would raise roughly $57.75bn–$64.35bn and implies a fully diluted valuation of about $1.40 trillion at the top of the range, making it one of the largest listings ever (https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/10/anthropic-sets-ipo-price-range-of-70-to-78-per-share-to-reach-an-implied-valuation-of-1-404-trillion).

Timeline: the final offer price is expected to be set on Wednesday, 18 November 2026, with first-day trading on Thursday, 19 November 2026 (https://ipo.anthropic.com/us/). Demand is reported to be around six times oversubscribed, and underwriters have reportedly weighed pricing above the $70–$78 range and a valuation above $1.5 trillion. Google, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft and TSMC have reportedly agreed to buy about $26bn of stock at the IPO price. Nasdaq's quote page for ANT lists revenue of $33.24bn for the first nine months of 2026.

The market backdrop is unsettled: the AI trade has come under pressure, with Nvidia down 4.3% on 12 November, about 11% for the week (a sixth consecutive weekly decline) and roughly $1.6 trillion of market capitalization erased since early October (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/13/nvidia-stock-jensen-affair-ai.html). On 13 November the Nasdaq Composite was down about 1.8% and the VIX stood near 21. Because ANT is a brand-new listing, no listed options or other market-implied price for late November yet exists, and there is no trading history to anchor the 27 November close.

Market calendar: US equity markets are closed on Thursday, 26 November 2026 (Thanksgiving) and close early at 1:00 p.m. ET on Friday, 27 November 2026 (https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/stock-market-holiday-schedule), so 27 November is the first session after the holiday.

`{"format": "llm_question", "info": {"sdk_version": "0.6.1", "rating": {"quality": 4, "ambiguity": 4, "resolvability": 4, "passes": true}}}`
items.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the closing price, in US dollars, of Anthropic, PBC Class A common stock (ticker ANT, Nasdaq Global Select Market) for the trading session of Friday, 27 November 2026, as shown in the "Close" column of the row dated 27 November 2026 on the Yahoo Finance historical prices page for ANT: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/ANT/history/. For example, a reported close of 94.20 resolves to 94.20. If Yahoo Finance does not display a closing price for that date, the Nasdaq historical quotes page for ANT (https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/stocks/ant/historical) will be used instead, and failing that, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).
items.fine_print: Friday, 27 November 2026 is a shortened Nasdaq trading session with a 1:00 p.m. ET early close; the official closing price of that abbreviated session is the value used. If ANT has not commenced trading on Nasdaq by 27 November 2026, or if no closing price for that date can be found in any of the sources listed above, the question is annulled.

items.question_text: Will at least one of the two Ir-192 sources stolen from the Rivers State radiography facility be publicly confirmed recovered by 28 November 2026?
items.background_info:
On 11 November 2026 the Nigerian Nuclear Regulatory Authority (NNRA) published a press release reporting a security breach at an industrial radiography facility in Rivers State: unauthorised access to the facility's radioactive source storage pit and the theft of six source projectors — two of which contained [Iridium-192 (Ir-192)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iridium-192) radioactive sources — plus one transit container. The exact date of the theft has not been disclosed; the licensee reported the incident to the NNRA in early November 2026, the regulator then notified the IAEA through its Incident and Trafficking Database, and the National Nuclear Security Committee (NNSC) met on Monday 9 November 2026 at NNRA headquarters in Abuja with national security agencies and stakeholders. That committee "agreed on modalities for investigating the incident and recovering the missing equipment" and assigned responsibilities among participating agencies. The NNRA has not named the licensee, and it has published no follow-up release, briefing or scheduled event on the incident as of 13 November 2026.

Nigerian outlets (Daily Post, Business Times, SkyNewsLink, OtownGist) carried the release on 11 November 2026 without reporting any recovery, arrest, suspect or the operator's name. An unverified OtownGist social-media snippet claims the devices were "recovered — fully intact" within 72 hours, but the accompanying OtownGist article of 11 November contains no such claim and the posts mix in unrelated content, so this should be treated as unconfirmed.

Background on the material: Ir-192 has a half-life of about 74 days and is the most common isotope used in [industrial radiography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industrial_radiography), where sealed sources of roughly Category 2 activity are used to inspect welds and pipelines. Such sources have little resale value and are dangerous if opened or scrapped, so stolen projectors are often dumped and later retrieved. Nigeria has a long record of source-control incidents (missing oilfield sources in 2003 that prompted an IAEA mission, a 2008 IAEA recovery mission, and a national search-and-secure programme running since 2010). The NNRA does publicise enforcement actions, inspections and recoveries on its news page, but on an irregular cadence — the archive runs to roughly 30 pages of items published weeks apart — and announcements frequently lag the underlying event.

The forecasting crux is therefore twofold: (a) whether the stolen Ir-192 material is physically retrieved by late November, given that roughly two to three weeks will already have elapsed since the theft was reported; and (b) whether the authorities publicise that retrieval within that period. A physical recovery that is never publicly confirmed resolves No, as does a public statement that only empty projectors or the transit container were found.

`{"format": "llm_question", "info": {"sdk_version": "0.6.1", "rating": {"quality": 3, "ambiguity": 3, "resolvability": 4, "passes": true}}}`
items.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, as of 28 November 2026 (23:59 UTC), Nigerian federal or Rivers State authorities (including the Nigeria Police Force) have publicly stated that at least one of the two Ir-192 radioactive sources stolen from the industrial radiography facility in Rivers State — the theft disclosed by the NNRA in its press release of 9–11 November 2026 — has been recovered, meaning the radioactive material itself is back under the control of the authorities or the licensed operator. A statement by the licensee or operator alone does not count, and neither does a statement that only empty source projectors or the transit container were recovered. The primary resolution source is the NNRA news and press-release page at https://nnra.gov.ng/nnra/news; if no qualifying statement is posted there, a report by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) attributing such a statement to those authorities also counts. The question is judged on the state of the public record at that cutoff, so the date on which a qualifying confirmation was issued does not affect the outcome; if no qualifying public confirmation exists as of the cutoff, the question resolves No.
items.fine_print: A statement reporting recovery of only some of the six projectors counts only if it indicates that the Ir-192 material was inside them (for example, that the recovered units were intact) or that the sources themselves were recovered. An arrest, a charge, or a statement that the material has been "located" or "traced" but not yet retrieved does not count; a statement that the stolen projectors were recovered intact, or that the Ir-192 material has been recovered or retrieved, counts as Yes.

items.question_text: How many confirmed U.S. measles cases for 2026 will CDC report in its November 27, 2026 update?
items.background_info:
2026 is the worst U.S. measles year in more than three decades. On its [Measles Cases and Outbreaks](https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html) page (update of November 13, 2026), the CDC reports 5,412 confirmed measles cases in the United States for 2026 as of November 12, 2026 — more than double the 2,289 cases reported in all of 2025 and the highest annual total since 1991. The 2026 tally includes 6 measles-associated deaths, a hospitalization rate of about 11%, 43 outbreaks, and 96% of cases among people who were unvaccinated or of unknown vaccination status.

Recent CDC weekly totals (data as of 12:00 PM ET Thursday, normally published Fridays): 3,294 (Sept 10), 3,659 (Sept 24), 3,886 (Oct 1), 4,852 (Oct 29), 5,182 (Nov 5, +330), and 5,412 (Nov 12, +230). [CIDRAP](https://www.cidrap.umn.edu/measles/us-measles-total-2026-tops-5100-cases) noted that the Nov 5 report marked the 13th consecutive week of triple-digit weekly increases, though the size of the weekly increment has fluctuated (a slower October was followed by a +330 jump, then +230).

The outbreak is concentrated in a few states. The [Pennsylvania Department of Health](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/health/newsroom/pa-department-of-health-provides-statewide-update-on-measles-out17) reported 1,505 confirmed cases across 45 counties as of November 9 (290 hospitalizations, 6 deaths, more than 11,000 MMR doses administered by its nurses), while South Carolina (about 670 cases), Wisconsin and Minnesota also have large clusters. CDC kindergarten MMR coverage data show several states far below the ~95% herd-immunity threshold (e.g., Idaho ~75%).

Other trackers publish different numbers on different schedules, which is why this question names CDC: the Johns Hopkins US Measles Tracker showed 5,400 as of November 6 (versus CDC's 5,182 for November 5), and PAHO's Situation Report #15 (November 6) reported 4,852 U.S. cases through epidemiological week 43. PAHO is weighing whether the region loses its measles elimination status.

The CDC page has updated weekly since 2025, sometimes shifting its publication day (Fridays, then Wednesdays from June 2025, then Fridays again during 2026) and labeling updates with the Thursday data cutoff; this question therefore keys on the publication date, not the cutoff. The remaining updates of November 2026 are expected around November 20 and November 27; Thanksgiving falls on Thursday, November 26, 2026, so the Thanksgiving-week update could be published early, published late, or cover a shifted data cutoff — and holiday reporting lags could depress its increment. A reasonable forecast centers on two further weekly increments of roughly 200–300 cases on top of 5,412.

`{"format": "llm_question", "info": {"sdk_version": "0.6.1", "rating": {"quality": 3, "ambiguity": 3, "resolvability": 4, "passes": true}}}`
items.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the national cumulative total of confirmed measles cases that the CDC reports for 2026 in the weekly update to its [Measles Cases and Outbreaks](https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html) page published on Friday, November 27, 2026, regardless of the data-cutoff ("as of") date that update uses. The value to be used is the page's national 2026 total — the figure in the statement "As of [date], X confirmed measles cases were reported in the United States in 2026," equivalently the 2026 "Total Cases" figure in the page's summary table — reported in whole cases (for example, the November 13, 2026 update showed 5,412 for 2026 and would resolve as 5,412). If no update is published on November 27, 2026, the first CDC update published after November 26, 2026 governs. If the page has since been overwritten by later weekly updates, the Internet Archive (web.archive.org) copy of the relevant update may be used to read the figure.
items.fine_print: Only CDC's own national 2026 total counts. Figures published by the Johns Hopkins US Measles Tracker, PAHO situation reports, individual state health departments, or news outlets do not count, even where they differ from CDC's. CDC's 2026 total includes confirmed cases among international visitors to the U.S. and cases reported by all jurisdictions, excludes probable cases reported by jurisdictions, and is subject to revision; the figure displayed in the governing update applies regardless of any later revision.

items.question_text: Will the CBRT's November 2026 Financial Stability Report devote a dedicated box to the 2026 fund liquidations?
items.background_info:
The Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye (CBRT) publishes its Financial Stability Report (FSR) twice a year. Per the CBRT's official calendar (https://tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/EN/TCMB+EN/Main+Menu/Announcements/Calendar), the next edition is scheduled for release on 27 November 2026. The most recent edition, FSR 2026-I (22 May 2026, Volume 42), runs to roughly 80 pages across five chapters (I. Overview, II. Global Financial Outlook, III. Non-Financial Sector, IV. Financial Sector, V. Non-Bank Financial Sector) and contained six numbered "Box" special-topic sections — Box II.1 (geopolitical risks and the credit market), Box II.2 (gold reserves), Box III.1.I (household deposits), Box IV.1.I (gold prices and credit conditions), Box IV.2.I (bank liquidity and loan pricing) and Box IV.5 (financial-market measures) — each listed by title in the report's contents (https://tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/dd2f6428-5ce2-434f-8e6f-ec48e7f9b281/Cover+Page%2C+Foreword+and+Contents.pdf?MOD=AJPERES). Note that box labels follow no single pattern: they appear as "Box II.1", "Box III.1.I" and "Box IV.5". Boxes are the vehicle the CBRT uses for a dedicated analytical deep-dive on a topical risk; Chapter V carried no box in May 2026.

The November 2026 edition lands two months after the largest fund crisis in Turkish capital-markets history. On 17 September 2026 the Capital Markets Board (SPK) ordered the liquidation of 131 investment funds managed by seven portfolio-management companies (Tera, Pusula, Hedef, Atlas, A1 Capital, Pardus and Bulls), alleging manipulation and inflated valuations. The funds held roughly TRY 1 trillion (about USD 20 billion) in assets as of mid-September and had 455,758 investors; the episode drove a sharp selloff on Borsa Istanbul, and the liquidation window was extended from three to six months on 20 September.

Official commentary so far has stressed containment. A CBRT research blog on 4 November 2026 ("Fund Liquidations and the Real Sector: What Do Firm-Level Data Tell Us?", https://www.tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/blog/en/main%20menu/analyses/fund_liquidations_and_the_real_sector_what_do_firm-level_data_tell_us) estimated that about 3,000 real-sector firms held TRY 116 billion in the affected funds (TRY 57 billion of it in money-market funds) as of 15 September — about 1.2% of the sector's total assets and 0.9% of outstanding commercial loans — and concluded the impact on the real sector was limited. S&P said on 20 October that the liquidation had not caused financial contagion and that household exposure was limited, while Fitch flagged risks at securities firms.

The stakes for the FSR are elevated because the affected industry is no longer peripheral: FSR 2026-I reported that the non-bank financial sector's share of Türkiye's total financial system rose from 12% in 2020 to 26% in Q1 2026, with investment funds at TRY 11.9 trillion (about 17% of GDP), 2,118 mutual funds by April 2026 and money-market funds at TRY 2.8 trillion as of end-April 2026. With no Monetary Policy Committee meeting in November (the next rate decision is 10 December 2026), the report is the CBRT's main financial-stability communication around this date.

`{"format": "llm_question", "info": {"sdk_version": "0.6.1", "rating": {"quality": 3, "ambiguity": 3, "resolvability": 4, "passes": true}}}`
items.resolution_criteria: This question resolves on the basis of the English-language edition of the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye's Financial Stability Report scheduled for publication on 27 November 2026, accessible from the CBRT's 2026 Financial Stability Report page (https://tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/EN/TCMB+EN/Main+Menu/Publications/Reports/Financial+Stability+Report/2026) through its "Click For Full Text" and "Cover Page, Foreword and Contents" links. It resolves YES if that report's table of contents lists at least one numbered box — any "Box" label format counts, e.g. "Box II.1", "Box III.1.I" or "Box IV.5" — whose title explicitly refers to the liquidation or winding-up of investment funds, to the Capital Markets Board (SPK)'s September 2026 action, or to the funds placed in liquidation. It resolves NO if no box title makes such a reference, including where the liquidations appear only in a chapter's body text or inside a box with a different title.
items.fine_print: A box whose title refers to investment funds generally, without referring to the liquidation, to the SPK's September 2026 action, or to funds placed in liquidation, does not count toward YES. If publication is delayed beyond 27 November 2026, resolution waits for the report to appear; the Turkish-language edition of the same report may be used if the English edition is unavailable. If the CBRT does not publish a November 2026 edition of the Financial Stability Report by 31 December 2026, the question is annulled.
